extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, literary critics, and serious readers of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making and evaluating the modern novel: how to select, shape, arrange and read material so that a coherent artistic book (not merely scenes or characters) is produced and appreciated. Emphasises reading 'aright', the novelist's selection/ordering work, and the critic's craft in reconstructing form.

rubrics_metrics.name: A book must have a form (shape)
rubrics_metrics.description: A book is a thing to which a shape is ascribable; the novel has a form even though it is revealed little by little and is hard to contemplate in completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the form is difficult to perceive (memory is fleeting and the book is experienced as a procession), critics and writers must treat a novel as a work with shape. The form may be approached rather than seen perfectly; recognising whether a book is 'shapeless' or well-proportioned is a legitimate critical task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism: the novel should be true, vivid, convincing — 'like life'
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is a picture of life and should be realized by the reader as true, vivid and convincing — like life, in fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first duty in criticism is to 'realize' the life presented; using taste, the reader then judges whether the representation is faithful and compelling. The capacity to turn flat impressions into solid shapes is fundamental to assessing fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, design and composition as artistic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form, design, composition are to be sought in a novel, as in any other work of art; a novel is the better for possessing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These artistic laws apply only loosely to literature (they are metaphors borrowed from visual arts), and while good design strengthens a book, novels full of life can sometimes triumph despite formal faults. Still, attention to proportion and design is a substantive evaluative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader must 'read aright' — cultivate critical reading to perceive form
rubrics_metrics.description: The beginning of criticism is to read aright — to get into touch with the book as nearly as may be; the reader must deliberately watch the book itself rather than only the life it suggests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading aright involves holding the novel at a distance so its form can be apprehended, resisting complete immersion in the fictional world, and actively reconstructing the book's shape page by page.

rubrics_metrics.name: The critic (reader) must become a novelist — actively recreate the book
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader of a novel (the critical reader) is himself a novelist; he must take his share of responsibility and recreate the book in his mind rather than passively receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author cannot transmit the exact work into the reader's mind; the reader must stand above the material, select and fashion impressions into a coherent object. This creative-reading is an effort requiring practice and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and arrangement of material are the novelist's primary tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist selects fragments from life, detects their significance, throws aside the accidental, re-makes them, and then directs the skill of his art to order and dispose them in a single embracing design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good fiction depends on what the novelist chooses to keep and how he orders it; critical judgment should ask whether the author's proceeding was the right one for the subject and whether a better development is conceivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and recognize the various narrative forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Different substances go to the making of a novel — the various forms of narrative, the forms in which a story may be told — and while many modifications exist their number is not infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and writers should learn these narrative forms (e.g., dramatic, pictorial, scenic, generalized) by close and conscious reading; current critical vocabulary is impoverished and needs precise use to identify methods and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle the material workmanlike: build impressions into structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The impressions that succeed one another as the pages are turned are to be built into a structure; the critic is missing his opportunity unless he can proceed in a workmanlike manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic must recognize fine variations, see components for what they are, and use them aright—like a craftsman knowing the properties of wood, stone, and clay. Emotional response alone is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the book from romantic scruple — analyse without fear
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a novel is a piece of life must not prevent the critic from taking it to pieces; in the study of the book as an ideal shape, it is important that one should be free from 'romantic scruple' about analysing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid shyness in criticism; analysis does not necessarily spoil the pleasure of a novel — the pleasure of creation can be greater than the pleasure of illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reader should hold fictional worlds at a distance to perceive art
rubrics_metrics.description: To recreate the novel in its right form the reader must keep the world of the book at a distance; no artist can be swayed completely by his material if he is to see the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires deliberate effort: resisting total immersion, maintaining critical detachment while re-creating the book's design and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge the author's choice of subject as a cardinal gift
rubrics_metrics.description: How a novelist finds his subject is beyond prescription and is his cardinal gift; the reader judges the novelist’s eye for a subject, but only after the subject is announced can other critical judgments proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the subject is given, exhortation or warning is pointless; once announced, critique assesses whether the author’s treatment and development serve the subject well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between novel-as-process (time) and novel-as-object (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel reaches us as a moving stream of impressions (a procession across time) and also should stand as a welded mass when complete; critics must navigate the ambiguity between these two aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation must account for both the temporal experience of reading and the retrospective perception of a coherent form; failure to treat both can lead to incomplete criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise which aspects are due to author vs. reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Many things the reader concretizes (characters, episodes) are created jointly: some failures may be the writer's (inadequate description) or the reader's (insufficient imaginative reconstruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should be aware of where responsibility lies: whether a scene's failure is due to authorial inadequacy or readerly inattention, and adjust judgment accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise critical language and develop a technical vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Our critical vocabulary is singularly poor; terms like 'dramatic', 'pictorial', 'scenic', 'generalized' lack fixed technical acceptation and hinder analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and writers should cultivate and use a more exact nomenclature to describe modes of narration and structural devices, derived from careful analysis of exemplary novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciate that fiction is both like and unlike other arts — use metaphors cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Words borrowed from the material arts (colour, perspective, composition) give hints about the method of the novelist but are only metaphors that cannot be closely pressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply such analogies cautiously: they can suggest methods (e.g., arranging material for relief and emphasis) but literature’s intangibility limits literal transfer of concepts from painting or sculpture.

rubrics_metrics.name: A book’s stronger elements survive; criticism may focus on authorial genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when detail is forgotten, the real heart and substance of a book (command of life, grasp of character) persist; criticism naturally tends to discuss the writer, his people, and his imaginative gifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical evaluation may legitimately foreground enduring imaginative effects (characterization, moral vision) as primary evidence of the novelist’s art, even if formal details fade.
